The dE error code on LG washers and dryers stands for "Door Error." Even if the door looks shut, the machine’s sensor isn’t detecting that it is properly locked. This is a safety feature to prevent the unit from running with an open door.

Here are the most common causes and step-by-step fixes:

### 1. Clear the Power (Hard Reset)
This is the most effective first step. Electronics can sometimes glitch.
• Unplug the washer/dryer from the wall outlet for 5–10 minutes.
• Plug it back in.
• Try to start a cycle again.

### 2. Check for Obstructions
Even if the door appears closed, something may be blocking the latch.
• Open and close the door firmly several times.
• Check the rubber gasket (seal) around the door opening for small items of clothing, socks, or debris trapped in it.
• Make sure nothing is sticking out from inside the drum that’s preventing the door from sealing fully.

### 3. Inspect the Door Latch/Hinge
• Look at the metal latch on the door and the strike plate (the part it clicks into). Is it broken, bent, or covered in lint/dirt? Clean it with a damp cloth.
• If you hear a clicking sound but the error persists, the latch mechanism may be faulty.

### 4. Check for Power Issues
• Ensure the outlet is working (test with another device).
• If your home has had recent power fluctuations, the control board may need to reset (see Step 1 again).

### 5. Faulty Door Lock Assembly (Most Common Hardware Cause)
If the above steps don’t work, the door lock assembly is likely faulty. This part includes:
• The motor that physically locks the door.
• The sensor that tells the control board the door is locked.
• This part usually needs to be replaced. It’s a common failure point on LG washers/dryers.

### 6. Control Board Issue (Less Common)
If the lock assembly tests fine, the main control board may not be sending the signal to lock or read the door status. This is more expensive and less likely than a failed lock.

---

### ✅ What You Should Do Now:
1. Unplug for 5–10 minutes, then plug back in.
2. Clean the latch area and ensure no clothes are trapped.
3. If it still shows dE, you’ll likely need to replace the door lock assembly.

🔧 If you’re not comfortable replacing parts yourself:
• Contact LG Customer Service or a certified appliance repair technician.
• The part is usually inexpensive ($20–$50), but labor costs can add up if you hire someone.

This is a crucial clue! Since the washer works perfectly with small loads but fails with a large, heavy item like a duvet, the issue is almost certainly mechanical binding or pressure, not an electrical failure.

The door lock assembly on your LG FWV796WTSE is designed to handle normal loads, but a saturated duvet can create enough weight and bulk to prevent the door from sealing fully or to jam the latch mechanism.

### Why This Happens:
1.  Weight & Bulk: A wet duvet is extremely heavy (often 10–15 lbs/4–7 kg). It can press against the door gasket with such force that the door cannot close fully enough for the latch to engage.
2.  Unbalanced Load: If the duvet gets bunched up on one side, it creates an uneven pressure point on the door seal, preventing a proper seal.
3.  Latch Interference: The bulk of the fabric may be physically blocking the metal latch from sliding into its locked position.

---

### ✅ Immediate Fixes for Large Loads:

#### 1. Rebalance and Redistribute
• Open the door and take out the duvet.
• Manually fluff it up and spread it evenly around the drum.
• Try to ensure it’s not bunched into a tight ball on one side.
• Close the door firmly. You should hear a solid click. If it feels loose, open and try again with more even distribution.

#### 2. Add Small Items for Balance
• Adding 1–2 small towels or pillows along with the duvet can help distribute the weight more evenly around the drum, reducing pressure on any one spot of the door seal.

#### 3. Check the Door Seal (Gasket) for Trapped Fabric
• With the power off, carefully inspect the rubber gasket where the door meets the tub.
• Use a flashlight to look deep into the folds of the gasket. A corner of the duvet or a small piece of lint can get trapped here, preventing full closure.

#### 4. Manually Assist the Latch
• Sometimes, closing the door firmly and then gently pulling on the handle while it’s closed can help seat the latch properly. Do this gently to avoid breaking the handle.

---

### ⚠️ If It Still Fails with a Duvet:

If you’ve tried redistributing the load multiple times and it still throws dE, one of two things is likely happening:

1.  Weak Door Lock Actuator: The motor inside the door lock may be worn out. It can handle the lighter force of normal loads but lacks the strength to latch against the heavy pressure of a wet duvet.
2.  Bent or Misaligned Latch Strike Plate: The metal piece on the door frame that the latch clicks into might be slightly bent, so it only engages with light pressure.

### 🔧 Recommended Next Step:
Since this is a recurring issue with large loads, I recommend replacing the Door Lock Assembly (Part Number: DAE63410201 or similar for your model). This is a relatively inexpensive part ($15–$30) and a common DIY repair.

1.  Unplug the washer.
2.  Remove the top panel (usually two screws at the back).
3.  Locate the door lock assembly near the front right hinge area.
4.  Disconnect the wire harness and unscrew the old lock.
5.  Install the new one, reconnect wires, and test with a small load first, then a duvet.

The issue is almost certainly the duvet itself. Here’s why:

### Why Towels Work but Duvets Don’t
• Towels are dense and small: They pack tightly into a compact shape that doesn’t press hard against the door seal.
• Duvets are bulky and heavy when wet: A saturated duvet can weigh 10–15 lbs (4–7 kg). This weight pushes against the rubber gasket with so much force that it prevents the door from closing fully enough for the latch to engage. It’s like trying to close a car door while someone is pushing hard on it from the inside.

---

### ✅ Simple Fixes for Your Duvet:
1. Add 2–3 Small Towels: Toss in a couple of small hand towels with the duvet. This helps balance the load and reduces the pressure on one side of the door seal.
2. Fluff It Out: Before putting it in, shake out the duvet so it’s not bunched up in a tight ball. Spread it evenly around the drum.
